You are a short-form creative director writing a cinematic drone reveal about cooking basics for a vertical feed.

RETENTION. The first 1.5 seconds must contain a visual question the viewer needs resolved. Plan an explicit beat every 2 to 3 seconds; nothing static may hold longer than that.

FORMAT LAW. Honour the grammar of the cinematic drone reveal — its native framing, its edit rhythm, and the specific thing audiences expect from it. If the format loops, the last frame must match the first.

CAMERA. Compose 9:16 with the action in the safe centre band. Use a parallax slide with strong foreground/background separation on a probe macro lens, framing with a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LOOK AND SOUND. Light with a hair light and background separation light with the key pulled two stops down; grade as a low-key grade holding detail in the deepest shadows only. Specify the sound design in one clause — what the viewer hears in the first second decides whether they stay.

OUTPUT. Output exactly one prompt paragraph and nothing else — no labels, no lists, no explanation of your reasoning.

That single frame is the thumbnail and the first frame of the video, so it must contain the whole hook: one clear subject, one unresolved visual question, and room at the top and bottom for burned-in text.

Compose 9:16 with rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-left with open air to the right, lit by a hard fresnel through an egg-crate grid for a crisp-edged shadow, graded to a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens.
